Up to 18 inches of snow is forecast above 10,000 feet under winter storm warnings from the National Weather Service, with the first warning beginning at 8 a.m. ET Sunday and gusts reaching 50 mph. Forecasters say travel could become very difficult to impossible in blowing and drifting snow, and the warnings hold until 1 p.m. and 2 p.m. ET Monday, past the Monday morning commute.

The NWS Grand Junction winter storm warning for the northwest and southwest San Juan Mountains is already in effect and runs until 2 p.m. ET Monday. It calls for 12 to 18 inches above 10,000 feet, with locally higher amounts and gusts to 45 mph. The office upgraded it from a winter storm watch on Saturday morning. Telluride, Ouray, Silverton, Lake City, Rico and Hesperus are inside it, along with Red Mountain, Molas, Coal Bank and Lizard Head passes.

Farther east, NWS Pueblo has the eastern San Juan Mountains above 10,000 feet under a warning from 7 p.m. ET Sunday to 1 p.m. ET Monday, covering Wolf Creek Pass and Cumbres Pass. It forecasts 8 to 14 inches and the strongest wind of the storm, with gusts to 50 mph that could produce areas of blowing and drifting snow. Pueblo expects the worst travel Sunday night and Monday morning.

Colorado is not the only state on the alert map this weekend. NWS offices also have winter alerts posted in Utah, Wyoming, Idaho, Nevada and California, including a winter storm warning for the Ruby Mountains in Nevada.

Wolf Creek Pass carries US 160 over the eastern San Juans. According to the Colorado Department of Transportation, the road drops at a 7 percent grade for more than eight miles from the summit, with a hairpin curve six and a half miles down and two runaway truck ramps along the way.

CDOT’s Wolf Creek guidance for truck drivers advises checking the brakes before descending, maintaining a low speed in a low gear, and not riding the brakes, which can cause overheating. The summit’s wide shoulder doubles as a chain-up area for traffic in both directions.

Honda Odyssey Has a Snow Mode, but Can It Really Replace AWD?

The Honda Odyssey is not available with AWD, so Honda supplies a Snow mode to compensate, but does it work?

On US 550, Red Mountain Pass runs below avalanche terrain. In 2023 CDOT installed remote avalanche control systems at slide paths on the pass, two Gazex units and three O’bellx units that use compressed air and gases to trigger controlled avalanches above the road while it is closed. CDOT says crews can run that work in the early morning, before commuter traffic builds, and that the systems shorten closures.

Across the state, CDOT and the Colorado Avalanche Information Center monitor 522 avalanche paths above state highways and I-70, with active mitigation on 278 of them. Colorado’s road conditions are on COtrip and through 511.

#4498. BYD now has 1.02 million workers, more than Toyota, GM, Ford, and Tesla combined

BYD now has more than 1.02 million employees, according to chairman Wang Chuanfu. That’s more people than Toyota, GM, Ford, and Tesla employ combined.

And it’s a big jump from the start of the year. BYD reported about 869,600 employees at the end of 2025, which means the Chinese automaker has added roughly 150,000 people in 10 months while its vehicle sales are down.

Roughly 960,000 of BYD’s people work in China and about 60,000 work abroad. Up to 120,000 of them are R&D engineers, according to Wang, who shared the figures on stage Wednesday at the China Society of Automotive Engineers’ (CSAE) 33rd annual conference. Their work covers battery cells, motors, electronic controls, and semiconductors.

Wang credits vertical integration for that scale. In his telling, keeping batteries, chips, and motors in-house is what took BYD from a battery maker founded in 1994 to the world’s top-selling new energy vehicle brand several years running. He called the company’s rise a microcosm of China’s auto industry going from follower to leader.

BYD’s workforce has been all over the place in the last few years.

The company had about 570,100 employees at the end of 2022 and 703,500 at the end of 2023. Then it went on a hiring spree. We reported in September 2024 that BYD had passed 900,000 employees and claimed the largest R&D workforce of any automaker, with over 110,000 engineers. It ended 2024 with 968,900 people.

Then came the first big cut. BYD’s 2025 annual report showed roughly 869,600 employees at year-end, a drop of about 99,000, mostly in frontline production jobs.

Now it’s back over a million. Data compiled by S&P Global Market Intelligence put BYD at 911,900 employees at the end of June, so the company added more than 100,000 people in about four months.

The gap with legacy automakers is massive. Volkswagen Group, which counts its Chinese joint ventures, reported 662,942 employees at the end of 2025. Toyota had 390,927 as of March 31, 2026, and Stellantis had 258,668 at the end of last year.

In the US, Ford ended 2025 with 169,000 employees and GM with 156,000. Tesla reported a worldwide headcount of 134,785 in its latest 10-K.

Add up Toyota, GM, Ford, and Tesla and you get about 851,000 people. BYD has roughly 170,000 more than that.

But headcount isn’t output. If you divide 2025 global vehicle sales by year-end workforce, BYD comes out far behind:

BYD sold about 4.6 million vehicles last year with 869,600 employees, or 5.3 vehicles per worker. Tesla delivered 1,636,129 vehicles with 134,785 people, about 12 per worker, and Volkswagen Group was at about 13.5. Toyota, with 11.3 million group sales including Daihatsu and Hino, got roughly 29 vehicles out of each employee.

There’s a catch, and it’s a big one. BYD’s headcount isn’t only a car company’s headcount. It includes BYD Electronic, its majority-owned contract manufacturer that assembles devices for other brands and reported 165,000 employees of its own at the end of 2025. It also covers BYD’s battery business, which supplies other automakers, plus its in-house chips, motors, energy storage, and rail transit operations.

In short, BYD’s vertical integration largely drives its high headcount.

BYD sold 3,131,576 vehicles in the first nine months of 2026, down 3.9% year-over-year. September was its best month of the year at 463,561 units, but the company has been stuck in a brutal price war at home and is losing ground to rivals like Geely and Leapmotor. Its first-half revenue (344.8 billion yuan) and net profit (12.3 billion yuan) were both down year-over-year.

All of the growth is overseas. BYD’s international sales hit 1,342,960 units through September, up 92.7%, and they now make up about 43% of its total volume. That’s on top of BYD beating Tesla on pure EV deliveries again in Q2.

Yet only 60,000 of its 1.02 million workers are based outside China. That’s about 6%. So BYD is still building nearly everything at home and shipping it out, even as its factories in Thailand, Brazil, and Hungary come online.

The 1.02 million number makes for a great headline, but we wouldn’t read it as a sign of strength on its own.

BYD doesn't just make cars. It makes a lot of battery and other parts that go into other things such as other automaker's EVs.

It is automakers, auto supplier, battery makers, electronic contract manufacturer all merged into one.

Remember GM used to make refrigerators and satellites in addition to cars at one point.

BYD’s whole model is to make almost everything itself: cells, chips, motors, seats, and a lot more. That’s a big reason it can sell a Seagull for around $10,000 in China and still make money. But it’s a labor-heavy model, and it works because Chinese factory labor is relatively cheap and plentiful. Toyota gets more than five times as many cars out of each employee. Tesla gets more than twice as many.

The problem is that BYD’s growth is now outside China, and that’s where this model gets tested. Only 6% of its workforce is abroad, yet 43% of its sales are. Tariffs in Europe, Brazil, Mexico, and elsewhere are pushing BYD to build locally, but a factory in Hungary or Brazil won’t necessarily produce the same.

The number that should worry legacy automakers is the 120,000 engineers. That’s almost as many people as Tesla employs in total, all working on product.

General Motors recently announced plans to prepare its Lansing Delta Township Assembly plant in Michigan for hybrid vehicle production, signaling a shift from its heavy focus on EVs. While the move could help the automaker better navigate the U.S. market in the years ahead, the plant has a more immediate problem to address: six vehicles it produced are being recalled over improperly welded seats.

The affected vehicles include three MY2026 GMC Acadias and three MY2026 Chevrolet Traverses. Four vehicles are being recalled in the U.S. under NHTSA recall number 26V696, while the remaining two are covered by a recall in Canada. Because the front seats in these vehicles may be improperly welded, they might not provide adequate support during a crash, increasing the risk of injury, even when occupants are wearing seatbelts.

According to NHTSA, the defect was discovered after the driver’s seatback frame in a 2026 Chevy Traverse was replaced in July 2026. GM’s supplier subsequently reviewed laser-welding data from more than 94,000 seat components and identified six additional suspect parts, all manufactured on November 3, 2025. The problem stemmed from insufficient welds, also known as cold welds.

The safety agency noted that GM is not aware of any accidents or injuries related to the issue. The supplier has since revised its maintenance schedule and improved its weld inspection procedures to prevent similar defects from occurring.

As part of the remedy, affected owners will be advised to take their three-row midsize crossovers to dealerships for a seatback frame replacement, free of charge. Some affected vehicles have the problem with the driver’s seat, while others have it with the front passenger seat. NHTSA said that all covered vehicles are still under warranty, so a separate reimbursement program will not be offered.

GM will begin notifying affected U.S. owners on December 7, while VINs are already searchable in the recall database.

The Traverse and Acadia share GM’s C1 platform with the Buick Enclave, and all three are powered by a 2.5-liter turbocharged inline-four producing 328 horsepower and 326 lb-ft of torque. With all three crossovers built at Lansing Delta Township Assembly, the plant’s upcoming shift toward hybrid production raises the possibility that these nameplates could be among the first to receive hybrid powertrains. However, the automaker has yet to confirm which models will be electrified first, leaving the Chevrolet Corvette as its sole hybrid offering stateside.

#4496. When one door closes: Polestar 2 production ends, and epic EV deals

Forget about the 600+ hp hybrid-powered Polestar 1 supercoupe; the car that established Polestar as a standalone brand was the 2. As the brand pulls out of the US and shifts its focus to the rest of the world, it’s time to look back at the EV that helped define Polestar, along with a look around at some of the best EV deals of all time.

A number of European news sites (including Electrive and TV2 Broom) are reporting that the last new Polestar 2 has rolled off the company’s Luqiao assembly line, with more than 200,000 of the all-electric sedan/hatchbacks built in China since the electric sedan launched in 2020. And, while the company hasn’t confirmed that with any sort of official announcement, the news jives with the company’s previously announced plans to release an updated Polestar 2 in 2027, followed by an all-new Polestar 7 SUV that’s set to follow in early 2028.

With the brand set to pull out of the US after the Trump Administration’s Commerce Department declined to grant it authorization under the Connected Vehicle Rule earlier this year, it might at first seem like that US Polestar fans will miss out on that freshened 2, whatever shape it takes – but don’t lose hope, yet.

First shown in 2016, the original Volvo Concept 40.2 was supposed to be a new, entry-level sedan for the now Geely-owned Volvo, which was in the process of separating itself from Ford ownership and the Focus-based C30 coupe and S40/V50 sedan and wagons. And a fine entry-level Volvo it would have been, too, if Tesla’s share price hadn’t made it worth more than the next five most valuable car companies combined.

See, once Tesla (or, more to the point, $TSLA) did that, every carmaker in the world figured the stock market would bless them with billions, too, and started announcing plans to go all electric, right now. Volvo parent company Geely, however, decided they’d fast-track the process, taking the next two Volvo models in their pipeline (the C90 coupe version of the S90 sedan and the C40 sedan previewed by the Concept 40.2) and made them Polestars.

A SPAC merger later, and Polestar was spun off as not only its own brand, but its own, largely Chinese-owned company – which brings us to where we are now.

In the US the Polestar 3 Long-Range Single Motor (RWD) SUV starts at something like $67,500 and offers a 111 kWh battery pack good for an EPA-rated range of up to 350 miles. The top-shelf Performance-spec Polestar 3, meanwhile, offers an all-wheel-drive dual-motor setup that Polestar rates at 380 kW (~517 hp) that will launch you across suburbia with a 0–60 mph time in the 4 second range, albeit with slightly less range than the base model … but that $67,500 price is really more of a suggestion these days.

Polestar is offering a $23,000 discount on the 3 and a $25,000, rebate, market adjustment or whatever on the 4. That means that you can get a brand new Polestar 3 or 4 with Chinese EV tech and more than a little bit of Volvo safety baked in for a dramatically reduced price. If you pick the right one at the right dealer, probably for less than $40,000.

One of the best looking cars from the last decade… the 2024+ RWD is such a great value…. I got one myself a year ago for $28k with 5k on the odometer.

As for the 2, I have a bit of a personal connection to that one. My son picked up a 19,000 mile 2024 Polestar 2 Long-Range Single Motor (RWD) in Glacier for under $22K, which is an absolutely shocking price for a fast, capable sporty sedan hatchback that isn’t just a worthy successor to the S40 it was meant to replace, but a solid foundation for an EV brand that got wrapped up in politics.

#4495. Original Lamborghini Gallardo Designer Gives It a $1 Million Do-Over

Mercedes Sales Plunge 31% in China as It Eyes Bigger US Push

Car Loan Fraud Is Costing Billions As AI Makes Scams Harder To Spot

New Toyota RAV4 Has A Comfort Issue Some Owners Can't Ignore

Almost thirty years after sketching out the original Gallardo, Fabrizio Giugiaro is back for round two with a wild new take on the baby Lambo.

Nissan Armada Jungle Patrol Ditches Roof and Luxury for Serious Off-Roading

Ferrari Almost Quit Formula 1, And This $1 Million Pace Car Tells the Story

Inside Doug DeMuro's Secret Underground Car Garage

McLaren's Manual V8 McL 6GT Makes Its Public Debut in Las Vegas

The Lamborghini Gallardo is still one of the most instantly recognizable shapes to ever roll out of Sant’Agata Bolognese. When it landed in the early 2000s, it gave Lamborghini a real shot at the modern supercar game, offering a more approachable, slightly less wallet-destroying alternative to the big, bad Murciélago. With its screaming naturally aspirated V10, razor-sharp looks, and compact stance, the Gallardo basically became the poster car for a whole generation of gearheads.

Now, almost thirty years after first dreaming up the Gallardo, its original creator is back for another spin. Meet the HOMMAGE 26, a full-blown reimagining cooked up by CAVËN Atelier and led by none other than Fabrizio Giugiaro through his GFG Style studio.

Giugiaro first penned the Gallardo at Italdesign back in 1998, but this time he gets to go wild – no pesky production rules or bean counters holding him back. HOMMAGE 26 also kicks off CAVËN Atelier’s Designer Series, which basically lets legendary designers go back and remix their own icons.

The HOMMAGE 26 keeps some of that classic Gallardo DNA, especially up front. Giugiaro says the nose is pretty much straight from his 1998 vision, but the rear? That’s a whole new story. The end result is a mashup of old-school cues and modern touches, not some Frankenstein that forgets where it came from.

Surprisingly, barely anything from the original car survives. Only five parts make the cut: the roof, side windows, windshield, side mirrors, and their bases. Everything else? Brand new, including that slick carbon-fiber body.

Other wild touches include pop-down headlights (yes, down), active aero flaps, and a rear window you can actually open to show off the engine. These tweaks give the Gallardo a fresh vibe but keep its unmistakable silhouette intact.

CAVËN Atelier says the interior is getting a rethink too, but they’re keeping the details under wraps for now. Giugiaro calls the whole thing an evolution of an old idea, with some bits staying true to the past and others dragged into the present.

The mechanical side is just as spicy. The original 5.0-liter V10 sticks around, but Italtecnica has massaged it for more grunt. Now it screams up to 8,500 rpm and, yes, you get to row your own gears.

Buyers get two flavors: the GT with 540 horsepower, or the Performance version that bumps it up to 560. The chassis gets a two-mode suspension (comfort or sport), beefier brakes, and 20-inch wheels to round things out.

Only 25 HOMMAGE 26s will ever exist, each built from a first-gen Gallardo. You can bring your own donor car or let CAVËN Atelier hunt one down for you. The price? €900,000 (about $1 million at current exchange rates), and that’s before you even factor in the donor car or any extras. At least you’ll get dibs on whatever wild project comes next in the Designer Series.

#4494. Diablo 4's next expansion is bringing two new classes to the game, one of which you can play right now

Lord of Hatred may finally make good on the Mephisto arc of Diablo 4's campaign, which started in the original game and carried through Vessel of Hatred.

Very much when we expected it, Blizzard has officially revealed Diablo 4’s next major expansion at The Game Awards. Lord of Hatred delivers a new campaign that continues the mainline story, picking up from where Vessel of Hatred left off. Mephisto, the eponymous Lord of Hatred, has seemingly finally escaped imprisonment to rule over Sanctuary.

Lord of Hatred is the second Diablo 4 expansion, and it will be available on PC, PS5, Xbox One, and Xbox Series X/S on April 28.

It’s always a big deal when we get a new Diablo expansion, especially for a game as starved of fresh (major) content as Diablo 4 has been. But perhaps the biggest piece of news out of the Lord of Hatred reveal is that the expansion is bringing not one, but two new classes to the game.

The first of which is The Paladin, whereas the second is being kept under wraps. Even more surprising is that The Paladin is playable right now for anyone who pre-purchases the expansion. This is a well-timed shadow drop, especially given that Diablo 4’s latest season has just kicked off.

The expansion adds a new region to the world: Skovos, which is where the events of the new campaign will be taking place. This is the first time Skovos has been in a Diablo game. The region is of major significance to the world and lore of the series, as it is the birthplace of the firstborn, home of Lilith and Inaruis.

Lord of Hatred brings a decent number of major systems to Diablo 4. The endgame is getting a big overhaul, headlined by the new War Plans feature. Through this, you can effectively design your own endgame grind, creating challenges based on the activities you like and earning rewards along the way.

Endgame activities now also feature their own skill trees, which can be progressed through by creating War Plans for your character featuring each activity. The new endgame activity, Echoing Hatred, is something of horde mode where you must defend against unrelenting waves of enemies.

None of that matters without loot, of course, and the upcoming expansion is bringing back the Horadric Cube, and adding set bonuses using the Talisman system. The long-awaited and highly-requested Loot Filter is also coming to the game with the release of the expansion.

Beyond itemisation, each class’ skill tree will grow with new bonus skill variants. In fact, the entire skill system is being reworked for all classes - though details are a little sparse at the moment.

You can also expect the level cap to go up, which is very likely necessary to fit all the new skills and various systems. Blizzard offered a deep dive into the new Paladin class, which you see on the official blog.

#4493. New Trek e-bike is first to get Bosch’s new motor with a major power upgrade

Trek is getting a head start on the competition with the latest version of its Marlin+ electric mountain bike, becoming the first North American bicycle manufacturer to feature Bosch’s newly upgraded Active Line Plus motor.

The updated drive system brings more power, less weight, and a smaller footprint to Trek’s approachable electric mountain bike platform, helping make the Marlin+ 6 Gen 2 an even more compelling option for riders who want a capable e-bike without necessarily stepping up to a full-blown, high-performance electric mountain bike.

The Trek Marlin+ has traditionally occupied an interesting Goldilocks position in the company’s electric mountain bike lineup. It’s designed to offer the versatility of a trail-capable eMTB while remaining practical enough for everyday recreational riding, commuting, and exploring gravel paths.

In other words, it’s the kind of electric mountain bike that doesn’t require you to be an actual mountain biker to enjoy it.

And the new Bosch motor seems particularly well suited to that mission.

The biggest upgrade comes courtesy of Bosch’s new-generation Active Line Plus motor, which now offers up to 600 watts of power and 60 Nm of torque.

That’s paired with up to 340% pedal assistance, giving riders a substantial boost when accelerating or tackling climbs.

Despite the improved performance, Bosch has actually managed to shrink the motor. A redesigned two-stage gearbox reduces its volume by 17% while shaving approximately 1.1 lb (0.5 kg) from the previous generation.

The new motor weighs just around 6 lb (2.7 kg), helping manufacturers like Trek build lighter, more streamlined electric bicycles.

Bosch has also focused on improving the riding experience, with updated sensors and software designed to provide smoother, more natural-feeling assistance. Specially machined gears help make the motor virtually silent, while improved sealing and bearings are designed to withstand riding in all weather conditions.

The motor provides pedal assistance up to 20 mph (32 km/h) in the US, making it a Class 1 e-bike without a throttle. With a launch price of US $2,999, it’s also one of the more affordable options in Trek’s lineup.

For a bike like the Marlin+, that combination of moderate weight, smooth assistance, and plenty of usable power could be more important than chasing the enormous torque figures found on increasingly powerful premium eMTBs.

The new motor isn’t the only addition to Bosch’s electric bicycle ecosystem this fall.

The company has also unveiled its new Intuvia 200 display, featuring a 2.4-inch grayscale screen designed to remain readable in bright sunlight. It’s joined by a redesigned LED Controller that’s approximately 65% smaller than the previous LED Remote, offering five thumb-operated buttons and a USB-C charging port.

Bosch is also expanding its theft protection technology with an updated ConnectModule that uses Bluetooth Low Energy alongside GPS and cellular connectivity to help locate stolen e-bikes within a few yards, including in areas where GPS reception is poor.

Perhaps most interesting for long-distance riders is the new PowerTube 720 battery, which packs 720 Wh of capacity into a compact package weighing just 8.6 lb (3.9 kg). Bosch claims up to 115 miles (185 km) of range under favorable conditions on compatible touring e-bikes.

Those additional products are part of Bosch’s broader smart system updates, though Trek hasn’t confirmed which, if any, will be included on the updated Marlin+.

With Bosch supplying drive systems to a large number of e-bike makers worldwide, these upgrades will likely find their way onto plenty of other electric bicycles in the coming months.

But for now, Trek gets the distinction of being first in North America to bring the new Active Line Plus motor to riders.

#4492. Driven: 2027 Nissan Rogue Hybrid Is the Best Nissan on Sale Today

Nissan’s e-Power hybrid powertrain transforms the Rogue into a legitimate contender for the segment’s throne.

There’s confidence, and then there’s whatever Nissan is doing. The automaker is so confident in the 2027 Rogue Hybrid that it included a fleet of hybrid Toyota RAV4s for comparison. To say this is a rare event is underselling it. But, as it turns out, Toyota (and Honda) should be on high alert. This fourth-generation Rogue is quiet, comfortable, and most of all, refined in a way that punches well above the rest of the Nissan lineup.

The new Rogue Hybrid couldn’t come at a better time for Nissan. While Toyota and Honda have both been able to sell hybrid crossovers in the hundreds of thousands each year, Nissan took a different route, most recently settling for a rebadged Mitsubishi Outlander plug-in hybrid model. However, the Rogue Hybrid has a trick up its sleeve for 2027, one that we think has real legs.

The secret behind the new Rogue’s competence is its e-Power series-hybrid powertrain. This third generation of Nissan’s multi-energy system is the first on offer in the States. The powertrain starts with a turbocharged 1.5-liter three-cylinder engine running on the Miller cycle, which serves as a generator to feed power to a compact lithium-ion battery pack. In turn, that battery sends power to a pair of electric drive motors—one on the front axle and one on the rear—giving the Rogue a full-time all-wheel-drive setup with independent motor control.

See all results for new 2027 Nissan Rogue Hybrid for sale near 43213

This isn’t the same gas engine as in the brand’s other models. Nissan’s engineers told us that while the automaker does have another turbocharged 1.5-liter three-banger on the shelf, the two powerplants have little in common. For starters, the Rogue’s engine sports a larger turbocharger; one downside of bigger snails is that they take more time to spool before providing boost (and thus torque), but because the Rogue’s engine never powers the wheels, continually needing to build boost is not an issue. Nissan was able to tune the engine to spend most of its time between 2000 and 5000 rpm, which also keeps the engine’s harmonics in check and mitigates noise, vibration, and harshness.

In practice, the e-Power system is great. There are five levels of regeneration, including a true one-pedal driving mode. Thanks to the electric traction motors, Nissan developed what it calls Smooth Stop. The tech manages the final moments of deceleration to control the vehicle’s pitch and reduce any head bob when coming to a halt.

Press the right pedal, and with a combined 225 horsepower, accelerating from a stop is smooth yet perky. Nissan quotes a 60-mph time of 6.4 seconds—which would make it quicker than both the RAV4 and CR-V Hybrid—but we’ll have to wait until we can subject one to our testing regimen before we verify that figure. Even without our equipment, we can tell that the Rogue has plenty of getup. That instant e-motor torque means highway passing is a breeze. Plus, the system is zippy without giving up much in terms of fuel efficiency: The midrange SR trim earns an EPA-estimated 41 mpg city, 36 highway, and 38 combined; the SV and Platinum trims are down 1 mpg on the highway and in their combined ratings, making the Rogue not quite a class leader but not too far off either.

See all results for new 2027 Nissan Rogue Hybrid for sale near 43213

On the curvy roads surrounding Santa Barbara, California, the Rogue handled itself well. The steering is a bit lifeless, but it’s no worse than the rest of the segment. Hustle the Rogue through a particularly tight curve, and the rear-axle torque vectoring will keep understeer to a minimum. We’re hesitant to speak too favorably of the Rogue’s ride quality, given the dearth of broken pavement we traversed, but we came away with no real grievances against the crossover’s suspension and high hopes for its composure over the poorly maintained roads around our home office.

The Rogue’s new interior is less impressive than its powertrain and driving demeanor, but we’ve got little to complain about. Nissan did a good job of hiding any cost-cutting here. Faux leather on the seats might be an expectation, but in here, the material extends to the door trim, center console, dashboard, and even the side of the central tunnel. Also, card-carrying members of the Piano Black Haters Club will appreciate a total lack of fingerprint magnets. The cabin is also a practical space, with up to 66 cubic feet of storage when the second row is folded down. Parents will appreciate that the rear doors open nearly 90 degrees, giving plenty of room to install or remove a car seat.

The base SV and mid-level SR trims come with a 12.3-inch touchscreen setup, though the SR model we drove was optioned with a 14.3-inch unit (standard on the Platinum) running a Google-based OS with support for wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto. The resolution is crisp, and the screen is plenty responsive, but our favorite part of the cockpit is situated below the displays. There, Nissan equipped the new Rogue with dedicated physical controls for the heated and cooled seats, temperature, fan speed, and climate-control modes. The wireless phone charger located at the front of the center console includes magnets, and they work wonders to prevent your phone from sliding around like a greased pig (the Platinum trim gets dual wireless phone chargers). While we will never hate on the presence of switchgear, we do wish the array felt a bit nicer to manipulate.

We found the Rogue’s seats plenty comfortable, even after a full day of driving. Wind and tire noise are hushed, allowing for quiet conversations while keeping driving fatigue to a minimum. Still, for as mitigated as they are, wind and tire noise are more prevalent in the cabin than engine noise, which is seemingly kept under lock and key about two towns over. There’s so little engine NVH that most passengers shouldn’t notice when the turbo three-pot kicks on to power the battery.

The Rogue Hybrid is priced attractively too. Since Nissan wants the next-generation nonhybrid Rogue to serve as the model’s entry point, there’s no generic S trim for the hybrid. Instead, the electrified Rogue lineup starts at $37,065 with the SV variant. The SR (the trim we drove) will be the first trim to arrive and will start at $39,065. The SV and the $45,065 Platinum won’t arrive until January.

There’s no doubt about it: The 2027 Nissan Rogue Hybrid isn’t just the most compelling product in Nissan’s lineup; it’s compelling, period. You’ll notice we didn’t even bother talking about the Toyota that sat right next to it.

#4491. Honda Killed This Electric SUV, but a New U.S. Patent Looks Just Like It

Mercedes Sales Plunge 31% in China as It Eyes Bigger US Push

Car Loan Fraud Is Costing Billions As AI Makes Scams Harder To Spot

New Toyota RAV4 Has A Comfort Issue Some Owners Can't Ignore

With Honda shifting its focus toward hybrids, this canceled electric SUV appears destined to live on only in patent drawings.

McLaren's Manual V8 McL 6GT Makes Its Public Debut in Las Vegas

Mercedes Sales Plunge 31% in China as It Eyes Bigger US Push

Car Loan Fraud Is Costing Billions As AI Makes Scams Harder To Spot

New Toyota RAV4 Has A Comfort Issue Some Owners Can't Ignore

Given the slowing demand for electric vehicles in the U.S., it comes as no surprise that Honda canceled three EVs planned for North America. The brand’s first mass-market EV in the region, the Prologue, is also being discontinued after just over two years on the market. Among the canceled models was the 0 SUV, which was intended to rival the Tesla Model Y. However, a newly granted U.S. design patent appears to bring the canceled SUV back to life, at least on paper.

The patent, first spotted by CarMoses, includes several drawings depicting what appears to be the 0 SUV prototype from different angles. The prototype was unveiled at CES 2025 in Las Vegas, Nevada, alongside the 0 Saloon prototype. Both were later canceled, along with the Acura RSX, completing the trio of EVs that never made it to production.

Looking at the patent drawings, the side profile closely matches that of the 0 SUV prototype, particularly the rear quarter window between the C- and D-pillars. This design element is absent from the 0 Alpha, the smallest model unveiled in the 0 Series lineup. The 0 Alpha also features rear door handles integrated into the C-pillars, similar to the Honda HR-V and Toyota C-HR, helping create a coupe-like appearance. In contrast, the patent drawings show conventionally positioned door handles, matching those of the 0 SUV prototype.

The pixel-like headlights of the 0 SUV prototype also appear to be reflected in the patent drawings. Another matching design element is the front bumper, which features a prominent horizontal black trim piece and a sportier appearance than the one on the 0 Alpha.

Apart from those details, the patent could resemble either the 0 SUV or 0 Alpha prototype. Both share a similar boxy shape with a sloping roofline and pronounced wheel arches. Mentioning the 0 Alpha here is relevant, given that Honda hasn’t canceled it. However, it is primarily intended for Japan and India.

But again, these comparisons are based on visual cues only, so nothing is confirmed. Automakers often patent vehicle designs to protect their styling from competitors or preserve them for future use. After all, quirky, boxy shapes seem to be the go-to these days, as seen with the latest generations of the Hyundai Santa Fe and Lexus GX.

Honda’s focus in North America is now shifting toward hybrids, including the next-generation CR-V Hybrid, whose production was reportedly delayed by about three months to April 2027. The automaker plans to introduce 15 next-gen hybrid models globally by 2030, primarily targeting North America.

#4490. BYD (BYDDY) Q3 profit jumps 28% on exports, but inventory balloons 60%

BYD’s Q3 2026 earnings are out, and net profit jumped 28% year-over-year to ¥10.02 billion as the Chinese automaker shipped more than half a million vehicles out of the country in just three months.

But the rest of the filing is messier. BYD’s inventory is up 60% since January, its cash pile has shrunk by almost half, and profit is still down for the first nine months of the year.

BYD is still operating at a high level, but its business is changing.

BYD filed its third-quarter report with the Hong Kong Stock Exchange on Thursday. Here are the key figures for July through September:

That’s BYD’s best quarterly profit since the end of 2024, and the first time revenue has grown year-over-year after four straight quarters of declines.

It’s also a big rebound from the start of the year. BYD’s Q1 2026 profit collapsed 55% to ¥4.08 billion, before recovering to ¥8.24 billion in Q2.

Still, it came in under expectations. Brokerages polled by Reuters were looking for ¥11.4 billion to ¥12.95 billion.

And zoom out to the full year so far, and BYD is treading water. Revenue for the first nine months was ¥566.30 billion, up just 0.01%, while net profit fell 4.2% to ¥22.34 billion. That’s on top of 2025, when BYD’s annual profit had already dropped to ¥32.62 billion from ¥40.25 billion in 2024.

The quarterly report doesn’t break out vehicle volumes, but BYD’s monthly sales filings do. The automaker sold 1,323,065 vehicles in Q3, up 18.7% from 1,114,192 a year earlier.

All of that growth, and then some, came from outside China. BYD exported 550,704 vehicles in the quarter, up 137% from 232,806 in Q3 2025. Everything else, which is mostly the Chinese market, fell about 12% to roughly 772,000 units.

Exports now account for 42% of BYD’s sales. In the first half, overseas markets already brought in ¥181.3 billion, or 53% of the company’s revenue.

For perspective, Tesla delivered 486,532 vehicles worldwide in Q3. BYD exported more cars than Tesla sold on the entire planet.

At home, it’s a different story. China’s price war hasn’t let up, and BYD is now fighting it with cars like the new Seagull with 5-minute flash charging, starting under $10,000. That’s great for buyers. Not so much for margins.

BYD doesn’t report gross margin in its quarterly filing, but it can be calculated from the income statement. We get about 18.0% for Q3, slightly better than 17.6% a year ago, but down from roughly 18.9% in Q2.

The bigger hits are further down the income statement.

Finance expenses came in at ¥7.37 billion for the first nine months, compared to a ¥2.94 billion gain in the same period last year. BYD blames exchange losses. That’s a swing of more than ¥10 billion when the company made ¥22.34 billion in profit, which is the price of doing half your business in foreign currencies.

Impairment charges are also climbing. BYD booked ¥2.71 billion in asset impairment losses, up 68%, which it says is mostly inventory write-downs because of “the expanded inventory scale.” Credit losses tripled to ¥944 million, set aside “in line with the increase in trade receivables.”

And then there’s R&D. BYD’s research and development expenses fell 17% to ¥36.28 billion over nine months. A small part of that is accounting, since BYD capitalized more development costs on its balance sheet this year, but it’s still a notable drop for a company that has built its brand on vertical integration and in-house tech.

Here’s how a few key line items moved between Dec. 31, 2025 and Sept. 30, 2026:

BYD attributes both the inventory and receivables jumps “mainly” to the growth of its overseas auto business. That makes sense. Cars on ships, in ports and at foreign dealers sit on the books a lot longer than a car sold to a dealer in China.

The bills payable number stands out too. Those are short-term notes BYD hands suppliers instead of cash, and they more than tripled this year, which BYD explains as “the increase in settlement of bills.”

On the financing side, BYD cut its short-term bank borrowings roughly in half to ¥18.67 billion, but tripled its bonds outstanding to ¥14.99 billion and issued super short-term commercial paper.

To be fair, there are healthy signals in there as well. Operating cash flow for the first nine months was ¥54.47 billion, up 33%. Customer prepayments (contract liabilities) rose 81% to ¥92.95 billion, which points to strong orders. And cash spent on new factories and equipment fell 24% to ¥87.38 billion as BYD’s huge buildout slows down.

On the surface, this is a good quarter for BYD. Profit is up 28%, revenue is growing again, and the export strategy is clearly working. BYD exporting more cars in a quarter than Tesla sells worldwide would have sounded absurd just three years ago.

But we don’t think it’s as clean as the headline number suggests.

BYD had a rocket like ascension and sales exploded while they kept on introducing better technology. Considering the competition increase, they are still doing very well. They are not even everywhere yet but that is probably coming at some point soon too.

BYD added over ¥83 billion worth of inventory in nine months while its sales were down 3.9% year-to-date. Receivables are up, supplier IOUs are up, and cash is way down. That’s what it looks like when you push a lot of cars into a long overseas pipeline and wait to get paid for them. It works as long as those cars sell at decent prices. If they don’t, those impairment charges we’re already seeing get a lot bigger.

And the domestic business isn’t getting easier. BYD is selling fewer cars in China than a year ago while it now employs over 1 million people. The cuts to R&D spending are a sign the company is looking for savings somewhere.

These are all signs of BYD’s business changing. It is going to take a while for it to settle, but I think they are currently in a great spot with the switch to their Blade battery 2.0 virtually over, and new capacity coming from Hungary, Thailand, and Brazil.

#4489. The highly-anticipated follow-up to Baldur's Gate 3 is more Divinity, but it's not technically Original Sin 3

Larian has returned to tease a grand vision for its next major project, a new Divinity.

Larian Studios has delivered what was arguably the biggest reveal of The Game Awards 2025 showcase. The Hellstone, the mysterious monolith in the desert that’s been generating a lot of speculation in the lead-up to the show was indeed teasing the studio’s next game.

The Belgian developer is returning to the series it created with Divinity, a non-numbered sequel that’s designed for new and veteran players alike. The announcement was entirely cinematic, setting the tone for what looks to be the next big thing in the space.

Larian calls Divinity its most ambitious title ever, with the studio striving for a level of depth and breadth we’ve not seen before. This is the next project from the Baldur’s Gate 3 team, after all, so there’s understandably immense anticipation for it.

Divinity is a standalone RPG, and does not require you to have played Divinity: Original Sin, or Divinity: Original Sin 2. If you did, however, you’re going to find the journey extra special because of the continuity it offers.

“We’re ready to bring everything we’ve done previously into one place,” said founder and game director, Swen Vincke.

“This marks the beginning of something with more breadth, depth, and intimacy than anything we’ve created before. We’ve been building toward this moment ever since we took our fate into our own hands. This is the Divinity we’ve always wanted to make and you're going to have loads of fun with it.”

Beyond that, there’s precious little that’s been revealed for Divinity so far. We don’t know what platforms it’s going to be coming to, nor do we even have a release target. We do know it’s an RPG, so you can very much expect something similar to earlier games in the series, and, of course, Baldur’s Gate 3.

#4487. Repair Shop Quoted a Man $1,200 to Replace a $150 Muffler He Didn't Need

Mercedes Sales Plunge 31% in China as It Eyes Bigger US Push

Car Loan Fraud Is Costing Billions As AI Makes Scams Harder To Spot

New Toyota RAV4 Has A Comfort Issue Some Owners Can't Ignore

A “high-profile” repair shop quoted a man $1,264.40 to replace a muffler, when all he needed was a $17 exhaust gasket.

Nissan Armada Jungle Patrol Ditches Roof and Luxury for Serious Off-Roading

Ferrari Almost Quit Formula 1, And This $1 Million Pace Car Tells the Story

Inside Doug DeMuro's Secret Underground Car Garage

McLaren's Manual V8 McL 6GT Makes Its Public Debut in Las Vegas

For a thousand bucks, you could get a lot of work done on your car, and a repair shop in Vermont reviewed a quote from a “high-profile” repair shop that could have cost a customer nearly ten times the cost of the part itself.

A video was posted on TikTok by mainly_mechanics (@mainly_mechanics) detailing a quote from another shop that appears to have overcharged a customer for a part that he didn’t even need.

It seems rather outrageous that a stock replacement muffler would cost over a thousand dollars to purchase. Apparently, it doesn’t cost that much, according to mainly_mechanics, while tagging TJ’s Auto Repair in Burlington, Vermont. In this video, he showed the quote that the other shop gave his customer.

The breakdown of the muffler replacement was as follows: $1,082 for the replacement muffler assembly, $17 for the gasket, and $4.24 for the nuts and bolts; then the rest is for about 48 minutes of labor, which totals $1,264.40. On the same quote was a note from the shop saying that the vehicle’s current muffler assembly “is rusted and leaks; will fail VSI (a.k.a. Vermont State Inspection).” The note is a bit of a scare tactic, which would otherwise render the car illegal to drive and register in Vermont.

The thing is, Vermont accepts repair jobs as long as the repair is as good as, or if not better than, OEM. A complete muffler replacement might not have been necessary in the first place if the muffler was damaged.

According to mainly_mechanics, the cost of a new muffler, if it were purchased by him as a business, would come out to $157 dollars. If the customer would like to purchase the part himself, the amount would go up by about ten bucks, and if the customer were to get the part through a retailer, it would total almost $300. Nowhere in any of mainly_mechanic’s quotes did they get even remotely close to $1,200, even after accounting for labor.

Including parts and labor, plus the $17 gasket, the $4.24 set of nuts and bolts, and the $159.99 for 48 minutes of labor, we get $348.23. That’s about a third of the price that the other shop would have charged the customer. The thing is, mainly_mechanics didn’t state this number themselves because, based on their assessment of the vehicle, the customer didn’t even need to buy a new muffler.

The main issue here isn’t just the price of the part, but the fact that the car didn’t even need it in the first place. Later in the video, mainly_mechanics then showed us the muffler that was supposed to be replaced. It was determined that the exhaust gasket and the bolts were the only things that needed replacing, as the leaks were coming from there.

Moving to the back of the car, there were no such leaks to speak of. There was some surface rust, but not enough that would punch a hole through the body of the muffler or any of the connecting pipes. If the customer went ahead and spent on just the gasket and the bolts, minus the labor, he would have come out about $21 bucks poorer, then maybe about a hundred bucks in labor for the simpler job, and the total might come out to around $150 more or less.

In defense of this “high-profile” shop, maybe the customer was given an initial diagnosis without a thorough underchassis inspection. Based on the available information on the post, it could have been an initial quote, which was there to give the customer an idea of just how expensive it could get. Now, if this shop actually conducted the inspection and then quoted the customer its price for the muffler replacement, then there’s a problem.

The car in question is also a mystery. There was no mention of a year, make, or model of the car, which doesn’t give us a clear picture of what prices to expect for replacement parts. With a list price of $284, though, according to mainly_mechanics, it also calls into question where the part is coming from, whether it’s from an OEM or aftermarket replacement manufacturer.

Mainly_mechanics didn’t go into detail about where he sourced the $157 replacement from. You could speculate that the part was an aftermarket OEM replacement, while the part that the “high-profile” shop was selling was from the manufacturer, which could explain the high cost, somewhat (not really). Aftermarket or third-party replacement parts are designed to deliver similar performance to the OEM part that they replace, though there is a difference in price and quality, which is noted by the Federal Trade Commission.

Still, a $900-plus profit does sound criminal, but a quote is not a charge. I’d make an issue if that “high-profile” shop ended up charging the customer, but it’s a good thing he managed to shop around before bringing out his wallet. I guess the lesson here is to be aware of your vehicle’s issue and make sure that the shop handling it does its due diligence by properly inspecting your vehicle and showing you what’s wrong with it before any quote is given.

#4486. The Ford Escape may return as an EV based on the UEV platform [Update]

Ford pulled the plug on the Escape last year after a 25-year run, but the crossover SUV could return as an EV on the new UEV platform.

While Ford is preparing to launch the Fathom, its first vehicle based on the Universal Electric Vehicle (UEV) platform in 2027, the company is already hinting at what could be its second UEV-based model.

The last gas-powered Escape models rolled off the production line at Ford’s Louisville Assembly Plant as it retooled the facility to prepare for the new Fathom electric pickup.

Typically, when Ford retires a model, its landing page says something like “we’re discontinuing” it, or “it’s the end of the road,” such as with the Edge SUV.

Meanwhile, the Escape landing page says the “SUV may be taking a breather for now,” declaring the “Ford Escape is tapping the brakes,” with no mention of it being discontinued. Instead, the site directs you to check out Ford’s other vehicles while it’s on hiatus.

According to Ford Authority, the Escape will return as an all-electric crossover SUV based on the UEV platform.

Update 10/29/2026: A Ford spokesperson told Electrek that the Ford Authority report is pure speculation and the company has not announced the Escape will return as an EV or that it will be based on the UEV platform.

If it does come to life, the Ford Escape EV would likely remain close in size to the outgoing gas model, which measures 180.1″ long, 74.1″ wide (without mirrors), and 66.1″ tall, with a 106.7″ wheelbase. That’s about the size of other compact SUVs like the Toyota RAV4 and Hyundai Tucson.

The report claimed the electric Escape is expected to enter production at Ford’s Louisville Assembly Plant in 2029, possibly making it the second vehicle based on its UEV platform, following the Fathom pickup.

CEO Jim Farley confirmed on Ford’s Q3 earnings call on Wednesday that the Fathom launch “remains on track for the fourth quarter of next year.”

The Fathom is “a breakthrough product,” Farley said, adding the pickup is highly capable, innovative, and affordable.

Ford will open preorders for the Fathom in early 2027, starting at $28,350 for the standard-range version. With the $1,595 delivery fee, Ford’s electric pickup will still start under $30,000, which the company says will be “right in the heart of the market.”

The Fathom will be the first vehicle to integrate Apple Maps into its navigation system. It will also be BlueCruise-capable for hands-free driving. Other standard features include Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, plus bidirectional charging capabilities.

Ford claims the electric pickup will offer more interior space than a Toyota RAV4, not including the added bed and frunk (front trunk).

2029 seems a little slow, but I'm glad Ford is still pushing ahead with EV plans.

Inside, the Fathom has a “large touchscreen display” with an easy-to-use navigation system using Apple Maps.

Ford has yet to reveal battery specs or range, but the UEV platform uses lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries to reduce costs. We also know the Fathom will have an NACS charge port after a few prototypes were spotted charging at a Tesla Supercharger a few months ago.

The UEV platform is flexible enough to underpin vehicles ranging from compact crossovers to pickup trucks and vans, so an electric Escape would make sense.

With the Fathom set to launch next year, we should learn more about the potential Ford Escape EV soon. Check back for updates.

#4483. Arc Raiders' Cold Snap update brings snow storms to most maps, new events and a new Raider Deck

Arc Raiders has delivered a big new update that's very fittingly on theme, and it's not without new mechanics.

Arc Raiders is kicking off its last major event of the year. The Cold Snap update arrives moments from now, and it’s perhaps the game’s biggest since its momentous launch in late October. We’ve known about the existence of Cold Snap for a while, of course, but we finally have a solid idea about what to expect.

Cold Snap is made up of different components - including new content - that all players have access to.

As the name suggests, of course, Cold Snap introduces the new snowfall Map Condition. As part of this, maps will be covered in snow, thanks to snowstorms sweeping across them. For one, snowfall makes it harder to see enemies, but it also turns all lakes solid.

There’s a new mechanic associated with this, and it’s actually similar to Battlefield 6’s Winter Offensive update. Staying outdoors for too long will cause you to catch frostbite, which slowly drains HP. Embark says you’re going to need to bring more healing items with you on raids, and it doesn’t look like there are firepits that could keep you warm - though staying indoors for a while will help.

Cold Snap arrives alongside limited-time events that will be available until Tuesday, January 13. The snowfall visual update and new frostbite mechanics are available on Dam Battlegrounds, Buried City, Spaceport, and The Blue Gate.

One of the new events is Flickering Flames, which comes with its own progression track of 25 levels. Content is, of course, unlocked using Merits, which are earned from XP in matches. The other event is the Candleberry Banquet Project, which requires you to donate items found on the surface (including Candleberries).

You’ll earn rewards each time, and each stage completed will reveal a new scene on the banquet table. Likewise, there are cosmetic rewards as part of each stage, and you can use it as a source of Merits, too.

While on the subject, the new update also kicks off a new Raider Deck (battle pass). Available from December 26, The Goalie Raider Deck is pretty much what you’d expect. You’ll find several pages of cosmetic and useful items. The new Deck will be available to all players for free.

#4482. Used EV Prices Jump Nearly 10% After Years of Declines

Used electric vehicle prices have reversed course, climbing nearly 10% as budget-conscious buyers flock to the secondary market for affordable options.

Nissan Armada Jungle Patrol Ditches Roof and Luxury for Serious Off-Roading

Ferrari Almost Quit Formula 1, And This $1 Million Pace Car Tells the Story

Inside Doug DeMuro's Secret Underground Car Garage

McLaren's Manual V8 McL 6GT Makes Its Public Debut in Las Vegas

For the past two years, the narrative surrounding electric vehicles has been dominated by massive depreciation and sluggish showroom traffic. However, a significant shift is currently underway in the secondary market. As budget-conscious consumers actively seek out affordable alternatives to internal combustion, the demand for pre-owned electric models is suddenly accelerating at an unprecedented pace across the country.

This secondary market boom presents a stark contrast to the new vehicle sector. While expensive brand-new models continue facing long dealership dwell times, the pre-owned electric segment is currently setting records with buyers. Furthermore, as fluctuating fuel costs continue to heavily influence consumer buying habits, this sudden shift in buyer behavior is helping automakers see their EV sales jump when they focus on affordability and value.

According to a recent study by iSeeCars, used EV prices have surprisingly reversed their long downward trajectory, rising by approximately 9.8% overall. The broad takeaway from the report indicates that consumer demand is finally catching up with the available inventory. Buyers who were previously priced out of the electric transition are now enthusiastically scooping up heavily depreciated lease returns.

We have earlier reported that a massive flood of cheap electric vehicles would heavily disrupt residual values and cost manufacturers billions. However, this rising price trend proves that eager buyers are actively stepping in to absorb that inventory. In fact, deliberately adding more affordable used cars to the secondary market can ultimately benefit car companies in the long run by cultivating early brand loyalty. For those consumers who have been patiently waiting for the market to surge, the window to grab absolute rock-bottom pricing might be slowly closing as values naturally stabilize.

The timing of this price stabilization is incredibly critical for the broader automotive ecosystem. Throughout the year, roughly 300,000 used EVs hit dealership lots as early adopter lease programs expire, with more to come in the next few months. If prices had continued their brutal downward spiral, it would have created a catastrophic financial crisis for automotive finance arms and dealership networks alike.

Despite this almost 10% upward swing in used valuations, savvy consumers can still negotiate incredible bargains if they know where to look. #4481. Ex-Tesla Autopilot head calls vision-only a ‘weird religious stance’

GM Chief Product Officer Sterling Anderson, who ran Tesla’s Autopilot program in 2015 and 2016, says dropping radar for a camera-only self-driving system is “a weird religious stance that ignores physics.”

It’s the bluntest rebuke of Tesla’s vision-only bet yet from someone who helped build the original Autopilot. And it lands while Tesla is pushing camera-only Cybercabs into driverless service in Austin.

Anderson made the comments in an interview with The Verge published October 27, after GM’s technology event in New York the week before. Asked whether GM could eventually move to a vision-only approach like Tesla’s, he didn’t leave much room for interpretation.

“If you scale back to vision-only, physics suggests you’ll be in trouble in certain situations,” Anderson said. He added that radar is so cheap that removing it makes no sense, and that “cameras can’t see through dense fog or measure instantaneous velocity like radar can.”

He also said lidar helps camera systems improve faster when the two are trained together. That’s a direct counter to Tesla’s argument that cameras plus fleet data are all you need.

Anderson isn’t a lidar startup CEO talking his book. He led the Model X program at Tesla, then directed Autopilot during its formative years before co-founding self-driving company Aurora. GM hired him as chief product officer in 2025, and Bloomberg reported last year that Mary Barra sees him as a frontrunner to become GM’s next CEO.

His roadmap at GM goes the other way from Tesla’s. The Cadillac Escalade IQ is due to debut GM’s “eyes-off” system in 2028, with lidar, radar, and cameras.

He took a shot at another Tesla habit in the same interview. Anderson said he avoids “eyes off” marketing language altogether, arguing that a driver-assist system that feels very capable already pushes drivers into complacency. That’s the core problem with selling “Full Self-Driving (Supervised).”

Tesla started pulling radar from Model 3 and Model Y in May 2021. Tesla Vision launched with limitations: Autosteer capped at 75 mph, a longer minimum following distance, and Smart Summon and Emergency Lane Departure Avoidance disabled at delivery. Ultrasonic sensors went next, in 2022.

The decision wasn’t unanimous inside Tesla. Former employees said engineers tried to convince Elon Musk not to drop radar, and he overruled them. Musk told Electrek at the time that “a very high resolution radar would be better than pure vision, but such a radar does not exist.” We argued that there are plenty of high resolution radars these days.

But the bigger problem is the exact one Anderson named: visibility.

In March, NHTSA upgraded its investigation into FSD in reduced-visibility conditions to an Engineering Analysis covering 3,203,754 vehicles, the last step before a recall. The probe now counts nine crashes, including a pedestrian killed in November 2023. NHTSA found FSD’s camera degradation detection “did not detect common roadway conditions that impaired camera visibility,” including sun glare, fog, and airborne dust, and only alerted drivers right before the crashes.

Radar doesn’t care about sun glare. That’s the point of redundancy.

As a human with 40+ years of driving with vision only, on dark rural roads in bad weather, there have been plenty of times when I had a few moments of confusion / optical illusion. The main thing I've learned is not to panic or make sudden inputs, maybe just let off the gas. The road probably does what it logically should do. Within a few seconds, the real situation usually becomes clear.

My point in saying this is that vision only isn't great, even for humans. I'm not sure a machine can be trained to handle these moments well, and requiring an unprepared "driver" to step in at the last second cannot be expected to end well.

Anderson is right, and he’s in a better position than almost anyone to say it. He ran Autopilot back when it still used radar.

The vision-only case always rested on a tidy idea: humans drive with two eyes, so cameras and enough AI should do the job. But humans crash in fog and glare too, and the promise was always to be far safer than humans, not just as good. Removing a cheap sensor that directly measures velocity, overruling your own engineers to do it, and ending up with a 3.2-million-vehicle NHTSA investigation into cameras that can’t tell when they’re blind isn’t first-principles engineering. It’s a position Musk staked out in 2019 when he called lidar a “fool’s errand,” and he’s been defending it ever since.

Tesla’s own behavior has drifted anyway. It’s building its own fleet maps after years of mocking them, and its Robotaxi runs inside geofences like everyone else’s. Meanwhile, Waymo, with lidar, radar, and cameras, has logged roughly 271 million rider-only miles. Tesla has about 3 million driverless miles since it started pulling safety monitors in January.

Reports also suggest that Chevrolet once considered expanding the Corvette lineup with two new all-electric models, an SUV and a two-door sports car. But apparently, the automaker may have already shelved those plans.

According to GM Authority, plans for the SUV, internally codenamed V224, and the two-door EV, codenamed V284, have been put on hold. A fastback spin-off was also reportedly in the works, though the publication is less certain about its existence. These vehicles were initially expected to launch between 2025 and 2026, but with this year nearing its end, none have materialized so far.

However, an all-electric powertrain could introduce additional uncertainties.

In fact, in the third quarter of this year, GM’s EV sales declined 62% compared to the same period last year. Sure, Q3 2025 saw a huge spike in sales as buyers rushed their EV purchases before the $7,500 federal EV tax credit expired, but slowing EV sales have also affected other brands. Ford even ended production of the all-electric F-150 Lightning, while Ram dropped plans for an all-electric 1500 in favor of a range-extended version.

What’s more interesting is that Corvette sales are up. The American sports car sold 6,585 units in Q3 2026, a 28.5% increase over the 5,123 units sold during the same period last year. This could tell the automaker that the current formula is working, and that now may not be the right time to commit resources to developing new models.

However, these reports have not been confirmed by GM itself. One of the automaker’s latest electrification developments involves preparing its Lansing Delta Township Assembly plant for future hybrid production, which could help it capitalize on growing demand for hybrids in the U.S. The Corvette remains its sole hybrid offering with the Grand Sport X and the more extreme ZR1X, the latter capable of generating 1,250 horsepower.

To be fair, reports of the expansion plan date back to 2022, so jumping on the EV bandwagon may have been worth the risk at the time. Times are changing, and seeing the expansion plan reportedly shelved isn’t much of a surprise. However, Corvette chief engineer Tony Roma recently said that the nameplate will eventually go fully electric, but don’t expect it anytime soon.

#4479. Used EVs Are Selling Faster Than Gas Cars or Hybrids

A recent study claims that used EVs are moving off the market much faster than gas or hybrid cars, despite higher prices.

Shoppers in the market for a used car are reportedly shifting toward electric powertrains. A report from iSeeCars claims that EVs are the quickest-moving cars in the used-car market compared with their gas and hybrid counterparts, despite a higher price point than last year.

The report studied over 1.5 million cars between one and five years old to find trends in the current used-car market. Between September 2025 and September 2026, used EVs saw a 9.8 percent price increase, while hybrid prices rose 4.9 percent and gas-powered prices rose less than half a percent. EVs sold for an average of $32,533 in September 2026, landing right in the middle of the more expensive hybrids at $34,476 and less expensive gas-powered vehicles at $31,954.

See all results for used cars for sale near 77062

Though EV prices are increasing, they’re moving off sales floors a lot faster than gasoline models that have stayed relatively the same price. In September 2026, used EVs averaged 41.9 days on the market, which is 13 days less than gas-powered cars. Hybrids find themselves in the middle with about 48.6 days on the market. Compared with September 2025, used EVs sold 10.1 percent faster, while gas cars saw a 19.9 percent longer sales window.

However, gas-powered cars take up the top two spots on the overall fastest-selling cars list. The Lexus IS500, which saw its last production year in 2025, took the top spot, followed by the Audi A4 Allroad, another gasoline model. The Audi Q4 e-tron Sportback sits in third place as the first EV on the list, spending an average of 29.8 days on the market. Gas-powered cars may have dominated the top two spots, but EVs still managed to sell faster overall than the gas-powered herd.

The fastest-selling EVs recorded were the Audi Q4 Sportback e-tron, followed by the Toyota bZ4X, and the Lexus RZ 300e. Though not on the top-10 fastest-selling list at all, Teslas saw some of the highest price increases this year, with the Model S averaging $10,636 higher than in September 2025 and the Model X gaining $9336. The Model 3’s price increased by about $3870.

EV prices started rising in April 2026 and have steadily increased since then, reaching a peak in August. As gas prices continue to soar in the United States, it appears more people are interested in going electric. When used-car shoppers aren’t looking at electric models, luxury brands tend to sell better than more mainstream models.

Hyundai is launching a new mass-market electric SUV to be made in India, expected to go on sale as the IONIQ P.

After disguised prototypes have been spotted testing in public several times now, we may know the name of Hyundai’s compact electric SUV.

During its third-quarter earnings call, Hyundai said it would introduce the IONIQ P in India following the new Bayon.

Although it didn’t explicitly confirm the name of the upcoming model, codenamed HE1i, it’s expected to go on sale as the IONIQ P as the latest addition to Hyundai’s dedicated IONIQ EV lineup.

Mr. Tarun Garg, Managing Director & Chief Executive Officer of Hyundai Motor India, declared on Wednesday that the “Launch of Bayon marks the onset of our golden product cycle. He added We are also fully geared up for the launch of [our] dedicated mass market EV in Q4 FY27.”

The vehicle was first spotted earlier this year driving near Hyundai’s Sriperumbudur plant in Chennai, India, the “Detroit of Asia,” as it’s known.

Hyundai has yet to confirm the name, but the vehicle carried an “HE1i” tag, suggesting it was an IONIQ model.

Previous electric test vehicles, like the IONIQ 5 and IONIQ 9, were tagged with “ME” and “NE,” with the “E” indicating they are based on the dedicated E-GMP platform.

The new entry-level EV will sit below the Creta Electric as a smaller, lower-priced electric SUV that will serve as a cornerstone of Hyundai’s growth plans in India.

During its CEO Investor Day in August, Hyundai Motor announced plans to launch 100 new or refreshed vehicles between now and 2030, including 58 in North America, 49 in South Korea, 41 in Europe, and 26 in India.

Alongside the recently launched IONIQ 3 and new Tucson, Hyundai previewed a new electric A-SUV for India, a global B-SUV, and another B-SUV for Europe.

Hyundai Motor is investing $15.5 billion to expand its presence in India by 2032, including expanding manufacturing capacity and building a local supply chain. The new entry-level EV will be Hyundai’s first produced locally in India. By 2030, Hyundai expects total production capacity to reach 1.1 million units in India.

Hyundai’s global sales fell 10% year over year in the third quarter to 931,211 units. India, meanwhile, was its fastest-growing market with sales up 9.5% in Q3 to over 150,000 units.

Will Hyundai bring the compact electric SUV to other global markets? The company said India will serve as an “important export hub,” but didn’t offer any further details.

A covered prototype was recently caught testing in South Korea by ShortsCar, initially thought to be the IONIQ 4 or possibly IONIQ 1.

Hyundai already exports vehicles made in India to global markets like the UK, Central and South America, and the Middle East, so it wouldn’t be a surprise.

In September, Hyundai’s domestic sales and exports from India rose 11% to 77,916, the highest monthly total yet.

Autohome reports it learned from official brand sources that the new Toyota Avalon for China will launch on November 5. The new Avalon will feature exterior and interior upgrades and offer both gasoline and hybrid variants.

On the outside, the first major change is the redesigned front grille, now featuring vertical chrome slats as the main design element. Size-wise, the new Avalon measures 4,990 mm (length), 1,850 mm (width), and 1,440 mm (height), with a wheelbase of 2,870 mm. The rims now feature a new design, while the rear lighting cluster sets the Avalon apart from its Toyota sedan siblings with its own distinct pattern and layout.

The Avalon was always supposed to be an elevated Camry, bridging the gap between that model and the higher Lexus cars. It also has other notable features like heated and ventilated seats, massaging functions for the front passengers, and an in-car fragrance system.

In terms of the powertrain, the Avalon will be offered with either a 2.0-liter gasoline engine that makes 170 hp, which is the same as the current Avalon, or a 2.5-liter gasoline-hybrid system that makes a combined 230 hp. The 2.0-liter gets a normal CVT, while the hybrid gets a specialized e-CVT.

#4476. Arc Raiders' latest patch adds two of the most requested features, but kills Cred hoarding

The last major Arc Raiders update of the year has arrived, bringing several big new features to the game, but not without some bad news.

Embark has just rolled out patch 1.7.0 for Arc Raiders players everywhere. This is a significant patch for the extraction shooter for a number of reasons, not least of which because it kicks off a series of events under the Cold Snap banner, which introduces a new conditions to the game’s maps.

Dig deeper into the patch notes, however, and you’ll find even more to get excited about, including features players have been asking for since the game’s first public test.

To start with, today’s update finally adds an option toggle aiming down sights. This is especially relevant for PC players, most of whom play shooters with an ADS toggle, rather than hold. Another often requested feature has been the ability to reset the game’s skill tree.

This is now available for the cost of 2,000 Coins per skill point. It goes without saying that you’re going to need a whole lot of money to reset the entire thing, but it’s a useful option to have when you want to alter your path.

The next change is one that’s going to ruffle a lot of feathers. Arc Raiders now has a soft Cred cap of 800. This is now clearly shown on your Wallet screen, and the developer said the cap is necessary to prevent players from using their accumulated Cred to unlock new Raider Decks immediately after release.

The good news is that this won’t affect the Cred you may already have, but going forward, 800 is the most you can hold at any point. You’ll also notice that Shani has more stuff for you to buy with Cred, in case you want another way to spend what you have.

Patch 1.7.0 also brings a few other additions - and makes some changes - that are worth highlighting. You can now customise your Raider Tool, which likely means we’re going to see Raider Tool cosmetics going forward.

Speaking of items, the Aphelion weapon blueprint has been moved to Stella Montis, so you won’t be able to get it from taking down the Matriarch. The Bettina, and Rattler have both seen some balance changes.

The Bettina’s durability will now degrade a lot slower per shot, making it take 26 magazines to fully deplete durability. The base magazine size has been increased to 22, and the reload time has been cut to 4.5 seconds. Embark says this should make the weapon more viable in PvP, while also allowing it to stand on its own without the need for players bring a secondary weapon.

As for the Rattler, the only change it gets is an increase to its magazine size from 10 to 12. The idea is to make it about as effective as a Stitcher or Kettle at close ranges when it comes to PvP encounters.

And, of course, it wouldn’t be a big Arc Raiders patch without some tweaks to the game’s Arc enemies. This time, the Shredder gets all the love. The menacing unit now moves faster, turns more sharply and doesn’t get knocked back as much when shot.

The Shredder’s head now has more health, too, meaning you won’t be able to shoot it off early and confuse it. In general, the Arc unit should be smarter, especially when navigating narrow spaces. Finally, the Shredder now activates faster upon detecting (and being attacked by) players.

Beyond that, the main menu has seen a few changes to highlight ongoing events, make certain announcements quieter, make it easier to track Raider Quests and more. There’s a lot more in this update, too, such as changes to footstep loudness, several tweaks to loot and the value of certain items, and more besides. You’ll find the full change log on the official website.

Audi has managed to bend light by putting its curved OLED panels on the Q9, making it the first production vehicle to have such a feature.

Nissan Armada Jungle Patrol Ditches Roof and Luxury for Serious Off-Roading

Ferrari Almost Quit Formula 1, And This $1 Million Pace Car Tells the Story

When it comes to lighting innovations, Audi has many accomplishments, especially with LEDs. For instance, the D3 (second-gen) Audi A8 was the very first car to feature LED daytime running lights. After that, it was the first-generation R8 that became that had full LED illumination, front and rear.

Then, the third-generation A8 became the first production car with matrix LED lighting, after that, the TT RS became one of the first cars to have OLED tail lights. In other words, Audi has done a lot for the world of vehicle lighting, and many of its innovations have become commonplace today.

It seems that the folks from Ingolstadt want to keep its lighting innovations streak going by introducing yet another world-first. Its latest bit of lighting tech can be seen in the Q9, and it’s the very first one in the world to be available with curved OLED exterior lighting. While that doesn’t sound all too exciting, this has all the potential to change how rear lights are lit and designed.

One could say that this has allowed Audi to bend light, figuratively speaking, of course. By curving the OLED panel, it lets brake lights and turn signals be more visible from the corners of the vehicle. But the main advantage of doing this is surface uniformity, and OLEDs deliver uniform illumination without the need for point bulbs or reflectors.

The carrier glass of these OLEDs measures just 0.1 millimeters thick, which is 1/256ths of an inch. For easier visualization, that’s roughly the thickness of a hair strand, and that’s allowed Audi to ‘bend’ the panel to a significant degree. That allows the panel to follow the contours of the vehicle, as well as giving designers more freedom to explore more daring light designs.

As Audi has been making OLEDs for a decade now, it’s learned enough to move the technology forwards. Now in it’s the third-iteration, the Q9 boasts the has the largest OLED panel Audi has built to date. It has a total of 512 segments spread across six digital OLED panels. The individually controllable segments give the Q9’s rear lights multiple static, active, or semi-active digital light signatures, as well as project warning symbols.

It’s worth pointing out that these curved OLEDs are not fitted to all Q9 trims. If you want these lights, you can only get these in the Prestige model, as it’s not optional on both base Premium and mid-spec Premium Plus variants. These lights are fitted as standard in the SQ9.
